accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE A level Mathematics subject content (Statistics, section O: hypothesis testing for a binomial proportion, the mean of a normal distribution with known variance and zero correlation using the product moment coefficient) and the Pearson Edexcel and OCR specifications' notation (H₀: p = 0.25, H₁: p > 0.25; H₀: μ = 500; H₀: ρ = 0, H₁: ρ ≠ 0). The lesson keeps H₀ a simple equality because the null distribution, e.g. X ~ B(n, 0.25), needs one value; H₁ is composite and fixed before data; expected counts n × p in the numeric items were checked at every parameter corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Every common examiner-report slip has a check: hypotheses written with the sample value (step 2 tiles 0.35, 0.52, 28/120; practice p1; mastery m3), statistic symbols in hypotheses (step 1 sort; step 5 x̄ and r pairs; challenge p̂ > 0.5; mastery m1, m2, m4), an inequality in H₀ or swapped hypotheses (step 5, challenge swap, m9), ≥ or ≤ in H₁ (step 5 μ ≤ 500, challenge p ≥ 0.1, tapping the H₀ point on the line), choosing the tail from the data (step 3 prediction, mastery m5), and a count in place of a proportion (step 2 tiles 21 and 26).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagnullh is built on writing hypotheses: a parameter/statistic tray sort, dragging a value into an H₀: p = [ ] slot from a context card, dragging <, > or ≠ into H₁ from the claim's wording, toggling the halves of a 0 to 1 number line either side of the H₀ point to shade H₁, and picking the one valid H₀/H₁ pair for a proportion, a mean and a correlation. No other flagship lab (flagbcrit, flagsimtest, flagbinp) states hypotheses; lab_distinct stayed under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner meets each rule by acting first: dropping 0.35 into H₀ returns '0.35 = 21 ÷ 60 is the sample proportion, a statistic. H₀ uses the claimed value of p'; dropping ≠ for a 'more often' claim returns 'The claim names a direction (more), so H₁ is one-tailed: p > 0.25'; shading both halves for p < 0.4 returns 'p < 0.4 is one-tailed: only below 0.4'; tapping the H₀ dot says H₁ never includes it. Done screens list the finished hypotheses together.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each hold the tempting wrong answer the step disproves: that H₀ should use the observed 13/40 (step 1 sorts it as a statistic), that a sample of 0.35 should set H₁'s direction (step 3 sets every sign from the claim's words), and that H₁: p ≠ 0.5 covers only values above 0.5 (step 4 needs both halves shaded). The done line repeats the learner's prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with ten distinct wrong-answer messages: two-tailed for a directional suspicion, p̂ in H₁, an inequality in H₀, x̄ for μ, ≥ in H₁, the wrong direction for a rival's claim, swapped H₀ and H₁, two-tailed for 'against sixes', and two wrong reasons for using p rather than p̂. The lab steps add per-tile messages for every wrong value, sign, shading and pair.

readability.evidence: Learner paragraphs explain one idea each with a worked context (a spinner that should land on red 25% of the time) and pass the readability limits in validate_lessons; the adult text was rewritten into short sentences after the first validator run flagged it. Precise terms are used throughout: parameter, statistic, null and alternative hypothesis, one-tailed and two-tailed, p, μ, ρ, p̂, x̄, r.

no_filler.evidence: The content gate found no banned phrases and the explanation stayed under 12% six-word overlap with every lesson, including Binomial probabilities, Judging binomial assumptions in context and the hypothesis-adjacent statistics lessons. Each feedback line names the value or symbol that is wrong and the rule it breaks.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (Android-size viewport, touch) in light and dark for all six steps after Show me: the tray labels were split onto two lines (Parameter / (population)) after the first screenshots squeezed them and the tray entries enlarged to 13 px; the H₀ slot, value tiles and sign tiles fit on one row; the number line shows 0 to 1 with the H₀ dot and both shading halves; the three pair cards stack without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: The browser gate completed every task with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge showed, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in light or dark. Every drag or tap has a labelled button ('p̂ = 0.35 from 60 spins: Statistic', 'H₀: p = 0.25', 'H₁: p greater than 0.25', 'Shade or clear values below the H₀ value', 'H₀: μ = 500, H₁: μ < 500'), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with every feedback line. Tile text is #3b0764 on #ede9fe and context cards are dark ink on #fef3c7 in both themes.
